descriptor.scene: TWO MEN AND WHAT THE WORLD GETS WRONG is the subject. GARY and DAVID KOBROSKY stand together at the lower LEFT, both in warm three-quarter view, sharing an amused look with each other, Gary in the light-wash denim jacket with the yellow smiley patch on the left chest and the orange pixel-mascot patch on the right chest. Filling the upper RIGHT two-thirds, a large soft painted thought-bubble holds the thing being described: an immaculate empty room, expensive identical chairs in perfect rows, a long polished table, tasteful plants, and NOT ONE PERSON in it, rendered slightly cooler than the warm real world below. The bubble's room is beautiful and dead. Keep the two men warm and the bubble cool.
descriptor._caption: The world starts to notice that the agentic startups that win keep naming the same room. Investors ask for it. Rivals copy the furniture. But a community is not furniture. It is ten thousand introductions that already happened.
